title: Console walkthrough — usage analytics & cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Summit Finance through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and line-item cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted API vs Dedicated for a customer-facing chat assistant; key concerns: latency, unit cost, data residency and auditability. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing models, SOC2/security pack, and schedule a Dedicated sizing call/benchmarks next week.
topics: Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2
action_items: Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Share detailed pricing spreadsheet and per-route cost model — due 2026-03-08
Priya Rao (Redwood SE): Run a sample benchmark (50 concurrent users, 1K token avg) on Dedicated profile and share latency/cost numbers — due 2026-03-11
Lina Park (Summit): Provide data residency and retention requirements + SOC2 questionnaire answers — due 2026-03-09
next_steps: Redwood to email pricing + security deck (link) after call
Schedule Dedicated sizing/benchmark session w/ Summit infra team (Priya + Todd) next week
Customer to review security docs and confirm procurement timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here. We got Priya our SE and Miguel on the line. Welcome Summit team.
[00:08] Mark Liu: Hey Alex, thanks. We just grabbed coffee — gonna jump in.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi all, quick agenda: we'll do a Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, show per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, then hit routing and security. Call should be 40-ish minutes.
[00:23] Sarah Patel: Sounds good. We're most interested in per-route cost visibility — we need to show finance teams exact unit economics for the chat assistant.
[00:29] Todd Greene: And latency; our SLO is 300ms p95 for the assistant.
[00:34] Alex Chen: Great — we'll show latency buckets in the dashboard and historical trends, and how batching/quant profiles affect cost.
[00:41] Priya Rao: Kicking off screen share — this is the Redwood Console. Top-left is the usage overview — tokens, requests, error rates. Notice the time selector — you can compare 7/30/90 day windows.
[00:55] Priya Rao: Here's per-route analytics — we break down by route name (e.g., /chat/assist, /embed/search). Each route shows requests, tokens in/out, avg latency, and cost attribution.
[01:12] Mark Liu: Quick question — how do you attribute cost per route when the same model serves multiple routes?
[01:18] Priya Rao: Good Q. We attribute cost by token accounting per request and model mapping. If two routes hit the same model, the dashboard prorates cost based on token consumption and any model-specific unit price. There's also an option to set custom weights if you want to override.
[01:33] Sarah Patel: Ok, and can we group routes by product or team?
[01:36] Priya Rao: Yep — tags and labels. You can filter and group by team, product, environment.
[01:40] Alex Chen: Also, the Console surfaces KV cache hits — so if you're using prefix caching for common queries we show cache hit ratios which reduce token cost. (note: some transcripts show K-V cash in audio).
[01:51] Todd Greene: That cache metric is key — our conversational sessions will get a lot of reuse.
[01:55] Priya Rao: Moving to cost breakdown — here's a per-route cost table. Columns: route, model, total tokens, unit price, compute adj (dedicated vs hosted delta), and total monthly estimate.
[02:09] Priya Rao: You can click into a route to see a trace of recent requests — token-level breakdown, prompt/response size, and latency waterfall.
[02:16] Sarah Patel: Is the token unit price fixed per model or can it vary by deployment (Dedicated cheaper)?
[02:22] Alex Chen: It can vary. Hosted API has per-token pricing; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with a different unit economics, and Optimize will suggest quantization and batching configs that change effective unit price.
[02:33] Mark Liu: We're concerned about accuracy — if we use quantized models, do we risk hallucinations?
[02:39] Priya Rao: There's always a tradeoff. Optimize provides quality monitoring — we tie prompt test sets to regression alerts. You can set thresholds and rollback policies in Console.
[02:50] Miguel Torres: We'll send a sample evaluation harness.
[02:53] Mark Liu: Perfect.
[02:57] Priya Rao: Showing the per-route chart — this one shows cost by bucket: token cost, GPU compute, and infra overhead. You can export CSV for finance.
[03:09] Sarah Patel: Does the export include model-version tagging? We need to show which model generated costs during a timeframe.
[03:15] Priya Rao: Yes, model versioning is first-class — we include model id, model version, quantization profile.
[03:21] Todd Greene: About SLOs — can the routing policy send low-latency traffic to a smaller model or Dedicated pool?
[03:27] Priya Rao: Exactly. Smart routing policies allow you to route by latency, cost, or region. You can set fallbacks: e.g., if primary model is overloaded, route to a cheaper or faster variant.
[03:38] Mark Liu: How are fallbacks instrumented? We need seamless traceability so we know when fallback occurred.
[03:44] Priya Rao: Each request includes routing metadata and traces — Console shows when fallbacks happen and what percentage of traffic used the fallback. You can drill into traces to see exact decision reasons.
[03:55] Alex Chen: (interrupt) Quick note on pricing: I'll send a hosted vs Dedicated comparison sheet. For many customers the tipping point is consistent throughput and data isolation — Dedicated reduces per-token compute if you commit capacity.
[04:07] Sarah Patel: Data isolation — we need VPC and KMS integration.
[04:11] Alex Chen: For Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering, customer-managed NAT, and KMS/HSM key wrap. Also audit logs and SAML SSO. We'll include SOC2 docs in the packet.
[04:22] Lina Park: On audit logs — are they immutable and how long do you retain them?
[04:26] Priya Rao: Console offers configurable audit log retention. For Private deployments you can ship logs to your SIEM; hosted has retention tiers as an add-on.
[04:34] Todd Greene: Any encryption at rest for cached KV stores?
[04:37] Priya Rao: Yes — KV caches are encrypted at rest and you can control keys via KMS.
[04:41] Mark Liu: Can we see a sample dashboard for a production route?
[04:44] Priya Rao: Sure. Here's /chat/assist — shows p50/p95 latencies, requests per minute, token mix (prompt vs completion), cost per 1k requests. Notice the spike at 02/28 — drilling in...
[05:00] Priya Rao: That spike was from a reindex job hitting the embed route, you can annotate events in the Console.
[05:06] Sarah Patel: Nice. That annotation feature will help our ops.
[05:10] Alex Chen: Let's talk about billing reconciliation — Console aligns with invoices and you can get token reconciliations for disputed charges.
[05:18] Mark Liu: Good. On the procurement side, what's the typical procurement timeline for Dedicated?
[05:23] Miguel Torres: From initial PO to capacity in about 4–6 weeks typically, depending on networking approvals for VPC.
[05:30] Sarah Patel: And SLAs?
[05:32] Alex Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs; hosted has best-effort with credits. We'll include the SLA doc in the packet.
[05:40] Todd Greene: We ran a quick POC with another vendor and they quoted a 20% lower price but no cache optimizations. Wondering where Redwood nets the savings.
[05:51] Priya Rao: A lot of the savings come from batching, KV caching, and model selection per route; Optimize recommends quant/profiles and autoscale configs that usually reduce unit cost without sacrificing quality. Also our runtime has attention kernel optimizations for long sequences.
[06:05] Mark Liu: Can we run a benchmark with our workload?
[06:07] Priya Rao: Yes — Action item: we'll run a benchmark using your typical session trace. Please share a sample of anonymized request logs.
[06:13] Sarah Patel: I'll get that to you.
[06:15] Priya Rao: Quick pause — any security red flags we should discuss now?
[06:19] Lina Park: Just need to confirm SSO, SCIM, and auditability for compliance. Also data residency in EU for some customers.
[06:28] Alex Chen: We support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, and you can choose regions for hosted model inference; Private gives on-prem options.
[06:35] Priya Rao: Back to Console — here's the rollouts page. You can do canary and A/B, track quality metrics, and auto-rollback on regressions.
[06:44] Sarah Patel: How do you define regressions? Strict BLEU or a custom prompt set?
[06:49] Priya Rao: Custom prompt sets. You define golden responses and acceptance thresholds; Console runs continuous evals and flags regressions.
[06:56] Mark Liu: Great, that's exactly what we need.
[07:00] Alex Chen: We also have an alerts page — cost alerts, token spikes, model drift. You can push alerts to PagerDuty or Slack.
[07:08] Todd Greene: We want a PagerDuty integration.
[07:10] Miguel Torres: We'll configure that during the pilot.
[07:13] Priya Rao: Quick demo of the cost modeling tool in Console — you input your routes, traffic profile, and it estimates monthly spend for hosted vs Dedicated. You can toggle model family and quantization to see delta.
[07:28] Sarah Patel: Can we include operational costs (support, storage)?
[07:31] Alex Chen: Yes — the tool has adjustable line items: support tier, log retention, and egress. We'll include those in the spreadsheet.
[07:39] Mark Liu: Any hidden costs we should watch for?
[07:41] Priya Rao: Egress and long-term log retention can add up. Also model training/evals external to inference are separate, but Console ties eval results into the platform.
[07:51] Alex Chen: (typing) I'll post links in the chat: pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 pack, and a sample benchmark playbook.
[07:58] Alex Chen: Link: https://redwood.app/share/pricing-summit (note: placeholder)
[08:04] Alex Chen: Link: https://redwood.app/share/security-soc2 (note: placeholder)
[08:09] Mark Liu: Thanks — we'll review.
[08:13] Sarah Patel: One last technical question — can you pin model versions per route and do partial rollouts?
[08:19] Priya Rao: Yes — pinning per-route is supported. You can also do traffic splits and canary percentages.
[08:25] Todd Greene: For Dedicated, what's the scaling story? We expect bursty traffic around EOD.
[08:31] Priya Rao: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity to handle spikes. We can set burst allowance based on instance headroom.
[08:40] Mark Liu: Any monitoring for model warm/cold start overhead?
[08:44] Priya Rao: Yes — Console shows model warm start latency and cold-start counts; Optimize suggests pre-warming based on traffic forecasts.
[08:54] Alex Chen: We're approaching the 45-minute mark — quick recap and next steps.
[09:00] Alex Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2 pack, Priya will run a Dedicated benchmark with your sample logs, and Miguel will coordinate procurement timeline.
[09:10] Mark Liu: Good. Targeting procurement approval by end of month if numbers look right.
[09:15] Sarah Patel: We'll share anonymized logs by Monday.
[09:18] Lina Park: I'll send our compliance checklist and retention needs.
[09:20] Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark session.
[09:24] Miguel Torres: Thanks everyone, speak soon.
[09:26] Mark Liu: Thanks, bye.
[09:28] (call ends)
